# ============================================================================
# Avature career sites, one `slug,host,section` triple per line.
#
# NOTHING HERE IS REGISTERED, AND THERE IS NO avature.go. The platform was
# probed far enough to say it is feasible and to leave the next person a
# measurement instead of a guess; the adapter itself was not written, because
# the session that got this far spent its remaining budget on iCIMS.
#
# PROVENANCE. The 87 triples come from the curated list at
# https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dtunkelang/job-search/main/slugs/avature_tenants.txt
# (downloaded 2026-07-28), whose header says each was verified live on
# 2026-06-18. The "~N" employer annotations are that curator's, kept verbatim.
# Everything after "PROBED 2026-07-28" is this project's own measurement.
#
# WHAT WAS MEASURED, 2026-07-28, one GET per tenant:
#
#   GET https://{host}{section}/SearchJobs/?jobOffset=0
#
#   87 of 87 answered HTTP 200 with at least one JobDetail link.
#   0 were bot-walled (the HTTP 202 empty-body challenge the upstream header
#     warns about) and 0 carried "Mandatory Login" or a FolderDetail redirect.
#
# That is a better result than docs/research/ats-platform-survey.md predicted
# and than the upstream list's own DROPPED section implies, and it is the one
# thing worth acting on: the runtime bot-wall and login-wall handling the survey
# says an Avature adapter "must" have was not needed by any of the 87 from here.
# It may still be needed from a different network.
#
# WHAT WAS NOT MEASURED, and must be before anything is registered:
#
#   * postings per request. The counts below are DISTINCT JobDetail hrefs on
#     page 1, not postings: Avature renders more than one anchor per posting on
#     some skins, so 6 links can be 6 postings or 3. The distribution is wide
#     (6 on 17 tenants, 30 on 13, 20 on 11, 120 on 2), which is either a real
#     per-tenant page size or an artefact of that double counting. Until it is
#     resolved this platform's cost per posting is unknown, and the survey's
#     estimate of 6-10 results per page would make it the most expensive lane in
#     the registry.
#   * pagination termination. jobOffset is an offset, not a page number, and
#     nothing here has checked what a past-the-end offset returns. That is the
#     single thing an Avature adapter must get right: this codebase has already
#     had an offset loop run 5,001 times against a board that ignored its
#     parameter.
#   * the canonical posting URL. It must be the tenant's own JobDetail page.
#     Several of these employers are large enough to also be in this registry on
#     another platform, and an apply URL pointing elsewhere is what caused every
#     double count found in this repo.
#   * the "stated total" recorded below is the first "of N" number on the page
#     and is NOT trustworthy: six tenants state exactly 999, which is a display
#     cap rather than a board size.
#
# ALSO WORTH KNOWING. The section is per tenant and not derivable -- the 87
# below use /careers, /en_US/careers, /campuscareers, /jobs, /en_GB/careers and
# more -- and one entry (tesco) is on the employer's own host,
# careers.tesco.com, rather than on *.avature.net. So an Avature key is a
# (host, section) pair, which is the composite-tenancy shape
# docs/research/ats-platform-survey.md warns about.
#
# Pacing when it lands: *.avature.net is one vendor backend and wants a shared
# limiter key, like *.icims.com. careers.tesco.com is a vanity front onto the
# same backend and belongs in the same key, which is what
# httpx.RegisterSharedBackend exists for.
#
# Format: slug,host,section  # upstream annotation | this project's probe
# ============================================================================
